import Hoare.While.Syntax
namespace While

inductive Ty
| num : Ty
| bool : Ty
deriving Repr, DecidableEq

inductive WellTyped : Expr → Ty → Prop
| num : WellTyped (Expr.num _) Ty.num
| bool : WellTyped (Expr.bool _) Ty.bool
| add : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.add e1 e2) Ty.num
| sub : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.sub e1 e2) Ty.num
| mul : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.mul e1 e2) Ty.num
| eq : ∀ e1 e2 t, WellTyped e1 t → WellTyped e2 t →
    WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) Ty.bool
| lt : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.lt e1 e2) Ty.bool
| gt : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.gt e1 e2) Ty.bool
| le : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.le e1 e2) Ty.bool
| ge : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.ge e1 e2) Ty.bool
| and : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.bool → WellTyped e2 Ty.bool →
    WellTyped (Expr.and e1 e2) Ty.bool
| or : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.bool → WellTyped e2 Ty.bool →
    WellTyped (Expr.or e1 e2) Ty.bool

theorem WellTyped.unique : ∀ {e t1 t2}, WellTyped e t1 → WellTyped e t2 → t1 = t2 := by
  intro e t1 t2 h1 h2
  cases h1 <;> cases h2 <;> rfl

def Expr.ty : Expr → Option Ty
  | Expr.num _ => Ty.num
  | Expr.bool _ => Ty.bool
  | Expr.add e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.sub e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.mul e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.eq e1 e2 => if e1.ty = e2.ty ∧ e1.ty.isSome then some .bool else none
  | Expr.lt e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.gt e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.le e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.ge e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.and e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .bool ∧ e2.ty = some .bool then some .bool else none
  | Expr.or e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .bool ∧ e2.ty = some .bool then some .bool else none
  | Expr.var _ => none -- typing not supported for variables yet...

open While

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For all expressions `e1` and `e2` and all result types `t`, if
    `Expr.eq e1 e2` is well typed at `t`, then there exists a common operand type
    `u : Ty` such that `e1` and `e2` are both well typed at `u`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Perform inversion on the derivation of
    `WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t`. The only constructor whose conclusion has head
    expression `Expr.eq e1 e2` is `While.WellTyped.eq`, and its premises are exactly
    `WellTyped e1 u` and `WellTyped e2 u` for some `u : Ty`; take this `u` as the
    witness. -/)]
lemma eq_typing_common_operand_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t : Ty} :
    WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t → ∃ u : Ty, WellTyped e1 u ∧ WellTyped e2 u := by sorry_using []

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every expression `e : Expr` and all types `t` and `u`,
    if `e` is well typed at `t` and also well typed at `u`, then `t = u`. -/)
    (proof := /-- This is exactly the uniqueness of typing supplied by the
    repository theorem `While.WellTyped.unique`, applied to the two derivations
    `WellTyped e t` and `WellTyped e u`. -/)]
lemma first_type_eq_second_type_of_two_typings {e : Expr} {t u : Ty} :
    WellTyped e t → WellTyped e u → t = u := by sorry_using []

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every expression `e : Expr` and all types `t` and `u`,
    if `e` is well typed at `u` and also well typed at `t`, then `t = u`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Apply `While.WellTyped.unique` to the derivation
    `WellTyped e t` and the derivation `WellTyped e u`. This gives the desired
    equality `t = u`. -/)]
lemma second_type_eq_first_type_of_two_typings {e : Expr} {t u : Ty} :
    WellTyped e u → WellTyped e t → t = u := by sorry_using []

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For all expressions `e1` and `e2` and all types `t1` and
    `t2`, if `e1` is well typed at `t1`, `e2` is well typed at `t2`, and there is
    a common type `u : Ty` at which both operands are well typed, then `t1 = t2`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Let `u : Ty` be the common operand type. By
    `first_type_eq_second_type_of_two_typings`, the derivations
    `WellTyped e1 t1` and `WellTyped e1 u` imply `t1 = u`. By
    `second_type_eq_first_type_of_two_typings`, the derivations
    `WellTyped e2 u` and `WellTyped e2 t2` imply `t2 = u`. Rewriting both sides
    through these equalities yields `t1 = t2`. -/)]
lemma operand_types_eq_of_common_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t1 t2 : Ty} :
    WellTyped e1 t1 →
    WellTyped e2 t2 →
    (∃ u : Ty, WellTyped e1 u ∧ WellTyped e2 u) →
    t1 = t2 := by sorry_using [
      first_type_eq_second_type_of_two_typings,
      second_type_eq_first_type_of_two_typings
    ]

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For all expressions `e1` and `e2` and all types `t1`, `t2`,
    and `t`, if `e1` is well typed at `t1`, `e2` is well typed at `t2`, and
    `t1 ≠ t2`, then `Expr.eq e1 e2` is not well typed at the result type `t`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Assume a derivation `WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t`. By
    `eq_typing_common_operand_type`, this derivation provides a common operand
    type `u` for `e1` and `e2`. Then `operand_types_eq_of_common_type`, together
    with the given typings of `e1` and `e2`, proves `t1 = t2`, contradicting the
    premise `t1 ≠ t2`. Therefore no such derivation can exist. -/)]
lemma eq_expr_not_welltyped_at_type_of_operand_types_ne {e1 e2 : Expr} {t1 t2 t : Ty} :
    WellTyped e1 t1 →
    WellTyped e2 t2 →
    t1 ≠ t2 →
    ¬ WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t := by sorry_using [
      eq_typing_common_operand_type,
      operand_types_eq_of_common_type
    ]

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For all expressions `e1` and `e2` and all types `t1` and
    `t2`, if `e1` is well typed at `t1`, `e2` is well typed at `t2`, and
    `t1 ≠ t2`, then for every type `t`, `Expr.eq e1 e2` is not well typed at
    `t`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Fix an arbitrary result type `t : Ty`. The lemma
    `eq_expr_not_welltyped_at_type_of_operand_types_ne` applies directly to the
    given typings of `e1` and `e2` and the inequality `t1 ≠ t2`, yielding
    `¬ WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t`. Since `t` was arbitrary, this proves the
    universal conclusion. -/)]
theorem WellTyped.not_eq_not_eq_ty {e1 e2 : Expr} {t1 t2 : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t1 → WellTyped e2 t2 → t1 ≠ t2 → ∀ t, ¬ (WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t) := by sorry_using [
    eq_expr_not_welltyped_at_type_of_operand_types_ne
  ]
